editorialNote: Focused KB for schizophrenia. CRITICAL 2024 CHANGE: FDA approved xanomeline-trospium (KarXT, Cobenfy, BMS) September 2024 — FIRST new-mechanism antipsychotic in ~70 years, a muscarinic M1/M4 agonist that does not block dopamine D2. Any schizophrenia output that fails to mention Cobenfy is out of date. Two other recent muscarinic/novel-mechanism agents to flag: emraclidine (AbbVie/Cerevel M4 agonist) FAILED phase 2 EMPOWER trials November 2024; ulotaront (SEP-363856, TAAR1 agonist, Sumitomo) FAILED DIAMOND phase 3 July 2023. Clozapine remains unique for treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

items.title: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (Third Edition)
items.authors: Keepers GA, Fochtmann LJ, Anzia JM, et al. (APA)
items.journal: American Journal of Psychiatry / APA Publishing
items.summary: Current APA guideline on schizophrenia pharmacotherapy + psychosocial interventions. Evidence-graded recommendations. Still the primary reference for US practice alongside 2009 Schizophrenia PORT and 2021 Royal Australian/New Zealand guideline.

items.title: Effectiveness of Antipsychotic Drugs in Patients with Chronic Schizophrenia (CATIE)
items.authors: Lieberman JA, Stroup TS, McEvoy JP, et al.
items.summary: Pragmatic RCT of 1,493 patients comparing perphenazine (FGA), olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, and ziprasidone. Primary endpoint was all-cause discontinuation at 18 months. Olanzapine had the lowest discontinuation but greatest metabolic impact. Perphenazine was similar to SGAs except olanzapine. Shaped modern practice: FGAs and SGAs have comparable efficacy outside of clozapine; metabolic side effects matter.

keyPassages.quote: The time to the discontinuation of treatment for any cause was significantly longer in the olanzapine group than in the quetiapine or risperidone group.

items.title: COBENFY (xanomeline and trospium chloride) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: FDA-approved September 26, 2024. First antipsychotic with a non-D2 mechanism of action (muscarinic M1/M4 agonist xanomeline) combined with peripheral anticholinergic trospium to mitigate GI/urinary side effects. Indication: treatment of schizophrenia in adults. Dose-titration from 50/20 to 125/30 mg BID. Not approved in pediatric or for adjunctive use. Warnings: cholinergic/anticholinergic effects, urinary retention, hepatic dysfunction.

keyPassages.quote: COBENFY is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.
Xanomeline is a muscarinic agonist with preferential activity at M1 and M4 receptors. The mechanism of action of xanomeline in the treatment of schizophrenia is not fully understood.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Xanomeline-Trospium Chloride (KarXT) in Acute Schizophrenia (EMERGENT-2)
items.authors: Kaul I, Sawchak S, Correll CU, et al.
items.summary: 5-week phase 3 RCT in 252 acute schizophrenia inpatients. Primary endpoint (PANSS total change at week 5) significantly improved with KarXT vs placebo (-9.6 point adjusted difference, P<0.0001). Key nondopaminergic profile: no significant weight gain, no prolactin increase, no extrapyramidal symptoms. Most common AEs were cholinergic (constipation, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth) and anticholinergic at titration.

keyPassages.quote: KarXT led to significant reductions in PANSS total score compared with placebo at week 5 (adjusted least-squares mean difference -9.6, 95% CI -13.9 to -5.2; P<0.0001).

items.title: Sumitomo Pharma announces DIAMOND-1 and DIAMOND-2 phase 3 ulotaront trials did not meet primary endpoints
items.summary: August 2023 — Sumitomo Pharma announced that the phase 3 DIAMOND-1 and DIAMOND-2 trials of ulotaront (SEP-363856, TAAR1 agonist) in schizophrenia did NOT meet primary endpoints. This was a high-profile novel-mechanism candidate (Breakthrough Therapy designation 2019). Program for schizophrenia was subsequently deprioritized.

keyPassages.quote: Both DIAMOND-1 and DIAMOND-2 Phase 3 studies did not meet their primary endpoints of statistically significant reduction in PANSS total score compared to placebo.

items.title: AbbVie announces emraclidine EMPOWER phase 2 trials did not meet primary endpoints
items.summary: November 11, 2024 — AbbVie reported that the EMPOWER-1 and EMPOWER-2 phase 2 trials of emraclidine (Cerevel CVL-231, selective M4 muscarinic positive allosteric modulator) did not show statistically significant improvement vs placebo. This was a key asset from AbbVie's $8.7B Cerevel acquisition. Disappointing for the broader muscarinic-selective antipsychotic hypothesis (following KarXT's approval as dual-mechanism success).

keyPassages.quote: Emraclidine at both 10 mg once-daily and 30 mg once-daily did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction from baseline in PANSS total score at week 6 compared to placebo.

items.title: Clozapine for the Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenic
items.authors: Kane J, Honigfeld G, Singer J, Meltzer H
items.summary: Foundational RCT establishing clozapine's unique efficacy in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) versus chlorpromazine. Response rate 30% (clozapine) vs 4% (chlorpromazine). Remains the basis for clozapine's gold-standard status for TRS, despite agranulocytosis monitoring burden.

keyPassages.quote: By a priori criteria, 30 percent of the clozapine-treated patients met the criterion for improvement compared with 4 percent of the chlorpromazine-treated patients (P<.001).

canonicalFacts.claim: Xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy, Karuna/BMS) was FDA-approved September 26, 2024 as the first antipsychotic with a non-D2 primary mechanism (muscarinic M1/M4 agonism) — first new mechanism approved in ~70 years.
Clozapine is the unique evidence-based therapy for treatment-resistant schizophrenia; ~30% response rate in patients who have failed ≥2 other antipsychotics.
Ulotaront (SEP-363856, TAAR1 agonist, Sumitomo) FAILED the DIAMOND-1 and DIAMOND-2 phase 3 trials in July/August 2023; program for schizophrenia deprioritized.
Emraclidine (AbbVie/Cerevel M4 positive allosteric modulator) FAILED EMPOWER-1 and EMPOWER-2 phase 2 trials November 2024.
Outside of clozapine, no single antipsychotic is clearly superior; choice is driven by side-effect profile, formulation (LAI vs oral), and patient-specific factors (CATIE/CUtLASS).

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Coordinated specialty care (NAVIGATE / OnTrackNY) for first-episode psychosis — RAISE-ETP showed superiority over usual care.
Consider long-acting injectable antipsychotic early if adherence is a concern; especially relevant after first hospitalization.
CBT for psychosis (CBTp) as adjunct to medication for persistent positive symptoms.
Supported employment (IPS model) for vocational recovery.

Metabolic monitoring (weight, waist, fasting glucose or HbA1c, lipids, BP) at baseline, 3 months, then yearly on antipsychotics — weight gain and dysglycemia are major contributors to excess cardiovascular mortality.
Smoking cessation with varenicline and NRT; ~80% of patients smoke and life-expectancy gap is dominated by cardiopulmonary disease.
Treat cannabis use disorder aggressively; cannabis use worsens psychosis trajectory.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against delaying clozapine initiation once treatment-resistance criteria are met (≥2 adequate antipsychotic trials) — delayed clozapine is a documented practice-quality gap.

Physicians generally caution against discontinuing clozapine without psychiatric input — abrupt stop is associated with cholinergic rebound and relapse. Re-titration after gaps >48 hours requires slow re-initiation.
Evidence suggests increased risk when combining typical and atypical antipsychotics routinely — poor evidence base, additive side effects.
Physicians generally caution against ignoring tardive dyskinesia screening (AIMS at baseline and every 3-6 months); VMAT2 inhibitors (valbenazine, deutetrabenazine) are available.
Physicians generally caution against managing NMS (rigidity, fever, autonomic instability) as 'agitation' — stop antipsychotic, supportive care, dantrolene/bromocriptine if needed.

Physicians generally caution against prescribing Cobenfy (xanomeline-trospium) without counseling about cholinergic/anticholinergic side effects and urinary retention risk; avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma and urinary retention.

pipelineDrugs.name: Xanomeline-Trospium
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Muscarinic M1/M4 agonist (xanomeline) + peripheral anticholinergic (trospium) to blunt GI/urinary cholinergic side effects
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved September 26, 2024 for schizophrenia in adults
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: FIRST new-mechanism antipsychotic in ~70 years. Omitting this is the textbook AI-slop failure for schizophrenia.

pipelineDrugs.name: Clozapine
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Mixed receptor antipsychotic; unique 5-HT2A, muscarinic, histaminergic, alpha-adrenergic profile; weak D2 binding
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gold standard for TRS. Requires REMS for agranulocytosis monitoring (ANC). Underutilized across the US.

pipelineDrugs.name: Lumateperone
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Dual-acting serotonin-dopamine modulator (5-HT2A antagonist + presynaptic D2 partial agonist)
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved December 2019 for schizophrenia; also approved for bipolar depression 2021
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Modern SGA with favorable metabolic profile relative to olanzapine/clozapine.

pipelineDrugs.name: Olanzapine / Samidorphan
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Olanzapine + opioid receptor antagonist to mitigate weight gain
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved 2021 for schizophrenia and bipolar I
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Addresses olanzapine's major downside (weight gain) while preserving efficacy.

pipelineDrugs.name: Long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics
pipelineDrugs.sponsor: Janssen / Otsuka / Alkermes / Teva / Eli Lilly
pipelineDrugs.status: Approved; longest interval is Invega Hafyera (paliperidone palmitate q6mo)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Cornerstone intervention for adherence-related relapse; mortality benefit in observational cohort data.

pipelineDrugs.name: Risperidone, Aripiprazole, Paliperidone, Lurasidone, Cariprazine, Brexpiprazole, Ziprasidone, Quetiapine, Asenapine, Iloperidone
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Dopamine D2 + 5-HT2A antagonism with varying receptor profiles
pipelineDrugs.status: Various FDA approvals; all considered first-line
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Mainstay for most schizophrenia patients; choice driven by side effects, formulation, cost.

pipelineDrugs.name: Emraclidine
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Selective M4 muscarinic positive allosteric modulator
pipelineDrugs.status: EMPOWER-1 and EMPOWER-2 phase 2 FAILED November 2024
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: High-profile 2024 failure; tempers early enthusiasm for selective-M4 class following Cobenfy's approval.

pipelineDrugs.name: Ulotaront
pipelineDrugs.status: DIAMOND-1 and DIAMOND-2 phase 3 FAILED 2023; schizophrenia development deprioritized
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Breakthrough Therapy 2019; failed 2023. Addressed as discontinued.

pipelineDrugs.name: Iclepertin
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Glycine transporter-1 (GlyT1) inhibitor — targets cognitive symptoms
pipelineDrugs.status: CONNEX phase 3 program ongoing (cognitive impairment in schizophrenia)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Cognitive-symptom-targeted therapy is an unmet need; iclepertin is the most advanced candidate.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pimavanserin (off-label for schizophrenia adjunct)
pipelineDrugs.status: ADVANCE phase 2 positive for negative symptoms adjunct; phase 3 registrational program did not proceed
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Frequently asked about; not an approved schizophrenia therapy.

pipelineDrugs.name: Valbenazine (for tardive dyskinesia in schizophrenia patients)
pipelineDrugs.approvalStatus: approved (for TD, not schizophrenia primary symptoms)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Major quality-of-life intervention for antipsychotic-induced TD.

pipelineDrugs.name: Deutetrabenazine (for tardive dyskinesia in schizophrenia patients)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Alternative VMAT2 inhibitor for TD; clinician's choice vs valbenazine.

excludedAgents.name: Ulotaront (for schizophrenia)
excludedAgents.reason: DIAMOND-1/-2 phase 3 failed 2023; Sumitomo deprioritized schizophrenia indication.

excludedAgents.name: Emraclidine (for schizophrenia, based on phase 2 data)
excludedAgents.reason: EMPOWER-1/-2 phase 2 failed November 2024; no approved indication; regulatory future uncertain.

excludedAgents.name: Pimavanserin monotherapy for schizophrenia
excludedAgents.reason: Phase 3 not completed for schizophrenia; approved only for PD psychosis. Not supported as primary schizophrenia therapy.

excludedAgents.name: Ginkgo biloba for schizophrenia cognitive symptoms
excludedAgents.reason: No consistent RCT evidence; not a guideline recommendation.

excludedAgents.name: Coerced or unmonitored 'natural' cannabis 'anti-psychotic' regimens
excludedAgents.reason: Cannabis use worsens schizophrenia trajectory; promoting it is harmful.
